text: The last raider retreats. For a moment, nobody celebrates. The hamlet is still standing; some of it is still burning.

speaker: Serra
text: Count the injured. The well is clear—keep a path open for water.

speaker: Road Warden
text: The families made it out. That child is with her mother now.
Perrin helps a shopkeeper drag a beam off the doorway. Rina checks the lanes for anyone left behind.
At the edge of the square, the child sits against her mother’s shoulder, quiet and shaking.

speaker: Kai
text: Are you hungry?

speaker: Child
text: I don’t think so.

speaker: Kai
text: Fair. I’m not sure I am, either.
He opens the cloth bundle Essa pressed into his hands. The last of the bread is a little dry, but the smell still takes him home.

speaker: Kai
text: Here.

speaker: Child
text: But that’s yours.

speaker: Kai
text: My mother would be furious if I didn’t offer. She’d somehow hear about it all the way from Oakstead.

speaker: Child
text: Is she really that scary?

speaker: Kai
text: Only if you’re someone she loves.
The child takes the bread. Kai waits until her hands stop trembling before he stands.

speaker: Serra
text: You ran at an armed man without a plan.

speaker: Kai
text: I noticed.

speaker: Serra
text: Next time, give me half a breath to make one.

speaker: Kai
text: Half a breath. I can try.

speaker: Serra
text: Try harder than you sound.
Perrin returns, sleeves dusty, wearing a grin he has not entirely earned.

speaker: Perrin
text: For the record, I meant to arrive with more dignity than that.

speaker: Rina
text: And yet we all survived the disappointment.

speaker: Perrin
text: That’s a very generous account of events.

speaker: Kai
text: You can argue while we walk. I’m Kai.

speaker: Perrin
text: Perrin. And I promise the horse is usually better behaved.

speaker: Serra
text: Serra.

speaker: Rina
text: Rina. We should leave before the smoke settles over the road.
They have a road in common for the moment. None of them knows what that will mean.
